limit: A track that holds a turnaround under one call sign with continuous ground reception is one flight-list row: the row names the track's first and last airports, and the distance-circle crossings, block times and stands at the middle stop are not on the row (the runway events there are still published as events).
Addresses such as 000000, 000001 or ffffff can merge several aircraft into one track; they are not flagged.
Only medium and large airports are candidates for the departure and destination airports.
Aircraft types come from the OpenSky aircraft database of October 2024.
A spoofed position that does not jump (a frozen position) still misleads the detectors.

Near areas of GPS spoofing a track's position can step by 5 to 20 NM and stay; a distance-circle crossing across such a step is kept when it passes one circle only and is marked info.position_jump, larger steps give no crossing.

Where reception starts at lift-off or ends over the threshold, no line-up, take-off roll, runway-vacated or precise take-off or landing time is published, because the aircraft had no report on the runway; the runway-window time (method legacy) is published from a report at most 1,500 ft above the ground.
One take-off and one landing time per track from the runway-window method, which gives about 60% of the times.
In-block times sit about 74 s after airport records given to the whole minute: the time is when the aircraft stops, which records of the minute place earlier.

When the transponder is switched on during the push-back, or the aircraft is first received already moving, the off-block time is the first movement received; pushes slower than 2 kt and stands with few positioned reports give late off-block times.
An arrival with no position or speed after the landing roll gets no in-block time.
A stand drawn in OpenStreetMap without a reference has no name; the block times and the flight list then name no stand.
Where a stand is drawn inside a larger stand area both passages are published; the larger one carries info.encloses_stand and the block times read the inner one.
Vehicles carry transponders; tracks that never leave the ground are marked info.ground_only on their surface events and get no block times.
A de-icing pad event means the pad area was passed; threshold-area events are aircraft on the ground near the threshold point, not the landing threshold crossing.
Aerial work that circles meets the holding definition; use info.context (arrival, en-route, other).
A crossing placed between two reports far apart in time (large bracket_s) is an estimate; FIR crossings use AIRAC cycle 524 for every day.
Tops on flights without a cruise are the highest report; one pair of tops per track; a top at the edge of reception has info.observed = false.
The cruise of light aircraft splits into many level-offs.

item: distance and time on tracks without positions
limit: A track without any position has no distance flown; its first and last seen come from its measured altitude or speed.
